races.name: Ronan & Tom Gibbons Memorial Apprentice Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Femme Beauty
runners_data.note: Showed a win at 11f on Good ground 12 days ago and rates the natural pacesetter here; the STYLE_FIT flag notes she is slightly out of her natural prominent role pushed to lead, but in a field this weak at OR 61 she likely takes it up by default and her recent Goodish-ground form is a genuine positive.

runners_data.name: Rose Sienna
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 2-year-old trained by J P Murtagh with a 247-day absence and only one run to her name, though that run was over a shorter 8f on Good ground — the step up to 1m1½f is a significant unknown, and the "fades in finish" flag combined with the layoff makes her a speculative hold proposition.

runners_data.name: Delusional
runners_data.note: Returned from a break 12 days ago to finish third over 11f on Good ground, which is directly relevant form for this trip and surface; he is a natural hold-up horse whose best effort came at this kind of distance, and the ear-blinds suggest he can be keen — one to follow once the field strings out.

runners_data.name: Zitkala Sa
runners_data.note: Holds a third-place finish over 10f on Good ground in his recent history and is a genuine closer by inclination, though he sits mapped into midfield here because the field is saturated with horses who want to come from the rear — his true run will come late, if he gets daylight from the two-furlong pole.

runners_data.name: Balance Of Trade
runners_data.note: Achieved a placing over 8f on Soft going which suggests he handles cut in the ground, but his more recent efforts have been disappointing and the OR of 48 reflects his limited profile; naturally a hold-up horse whose position on the map understates how far back he'll likely be tracking at the top of the straight.

runners_data.name: Cameclose
runners_data.note: Trained by Jack W Davison who has had no winners in the past 14 days from six runners, and this horse carries the "fades in finish" flag alongside a sequence of 88-499 — the blinkered headgear hasn't unlocked a finish yet, and being a true closer in a field full of closers means he is likely to be further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Kart Of Gold
runners_data.note: A flat form string of 70090 with the "fades in finish" alert says everything about his reliability as a finisher; trained by Adrian McGuinness who has been busy but at 2/26 in 14 days, and the horse's 21-day absence without any promising recent effort at 10f makes it hard to construct a winning case.

runners_data.name: Music And Song
runners_data.note: Lowest OR in the field at 40, with Thomas Dowling sending out just one runner in 14 days (won), and a form string of 09960 that includes a blank — the apprentice rider Jack Cleary will need to execute well from the rear to get anything from this horse, who has shown little evidence of a finish on any surface or trip.

races.paceDynamic: Femme Beauty is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 8-runner apprentice claimer over 1m1½f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is set to control the pace entirely from the front without pressure. The remainder of the field — Zitkala Sa, Cameclose, Balance Of Trade, Kart Of Gold, and Music And Song — are all natural hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because there are simply too many hold-up horses to fill the rear naturally; of those, Femme Beauty is the only one who will realistically dictate from the front, with Rose Sienna and Delusional the most likely to fill early prominent slots behind her. On Good to Yielding ground over this mid-distance trip, a lone front-runner setting a sustainable gallop without pressure will tend to find it difficult to be picked off if she conserves enough energy through the middle stages, and the fractured hold-up brigade will be navigating their way through midfield traffic rather than launching from an ideal position. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with genuine finishing ability who can thread through from midfield in the straight, though the redistribution caveat means many of those types may not be operating from their true comfort zone — making Femme Beauty's controlled lead a meaningful tactical asset.

scenarios.body: If Femme Beauty sets a pace that proves too strong for her own stamina and one of the prominent-tracking horses challenges before the final furlong.

scenarios.trigger: If pace is erratic, jockeys in the apprentice field misjudge positions, and the race breaks up into a bunched sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If pace is erratic, jockeys in the apprentice field misjudge positions, and the race breaks up into a bunched sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Femme Beauty is the only confirmed pace-setter — if she jumps and leads without challenge, watch whether the apprentice jockey Max Popan (7lb claimer) can manage the pace sensibly through the early stages, as over- or under-cooking the gallop will dictate whether she holds on or gets caught.

The field contains seven apprentice riders including multiple claiming allowances — positional errors, tight gaps and bunching through the Ballinrobe bend are a genuine risk that could compromise hold-up horses like Zitkala Sa and Delusional who need clear running.

Rose Sienna returns from a 247-day layoff for J P Murtagh — if she shows market support or moves stylishly in the paddock, it may signal stable confidence in a horse whose single run gave little to work with form-wise.

Good to Yielding ground across the whole card at Ballinrobe — all seven races on the same surface — means no meaningful going change to monitor within this race, but note that the going is softer than the nominal "Good to Soft" in the race header, which will test the stamina reserves of the hold-up brigade coming late.

Cameclose runs just 8 days after its last start, a notably quick turnaround for a horse already flagged as fading in finishes — watch for any sign of freshness or stiffness in the pre-race warmup that might indicate the quick return is a negative rather than a sign of stable confidence.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Median Auction Maiden (Median Auction Race)
Lodge At Ashford Castle Maiden

runners_data.name: Believe Again
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator with a fade pattern at the finish; trainer Seamus O'Donnell has one run in 14 days and the 35-day break adds a fitness query, while being mapped to midfield understates how far back this horse will actually race — discounted in most pace shapes here.

runners_data.name: Big Dispute
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with solid form at the each-way level on similar going (1W5P from 13 similar-going starts), stays well and handles cut; Kevin Coleman's runner likely settles mid-to-rear and needs a strong gallop to get competitive, which is not guaranteed here.

runners_data.name: Coul Dreamer
runners_data.note: W McCreery's five-year-old is a natural rear-runner who will be squeezed for space with multiple hold-up types in this field; the 18-day turnaround is fine and there is placed form on softer ground, but at OR 73 the class ceiling may be reached before the finish.

runners_data.name: If Not For Grace
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes the ride on this lightly-exposed four-year-old, but the sole run was a well-beaten 15th on good ground, and the fade-in-finish flag reinforces that this is a horse who will hit a wall rather than power home — needs a career-best to get involved.

runners_data.name: Mano Chicago
runners_data.note: The race's lone pace-setter ridden by Ben Coen for JP Murtagh; holds an OR of 80, is proven on similar going (0W4P from 7 similar-going starts), and wears a hood — likely to control the tempo entirely from flag fall and make this a test of who can sit closest.

runners_data.name: Mischievous Fun
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery rides and trains; two career runs both on good ground over longer trips resulted in double-figure finishes, the fade flag is prominent, and the 44-day jumps absence adds a significant freshness doubt for a horse yet to show maiden-quality form.

runners_data.name: Take Me
runners_data.note: Colin Keane steps in for Noel Meade's four-year-old who wears a tongue-tie and has an unknown-style flag — placed at 9f on heavy and ran respectably on good ground, so the step to 1m1½f and this surface looks workable; Keane's tactical intelligence is a significant asset in a race with a lone leader.

runners_data.name: Western Bandit
runners_data.note: Shane Foley's mount is a genuine hold-up horse by nature wearing a tongue-tie, tucked into midfield only because the rear is oversubscribed; four runs without a place on this trip/going combination, and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 confirms it cannot realistically secure its preferred position.

runners_data.name: Cuckaloo Hill
runners_data.note: Leigh Roche partners this four-year-old who carries a tongue-tie and a fade flag and is tagged as a true hold-up horse forced into midfield; OR 46 represents the lowest class in the field and recent form figures of 8-0400 offer little encouragement for a competitive effort.

runners_data.name: Drowsy Maggie
runners_data.note: Nathan Crosse rides this unraced four-year-old for Gerard Kyne who has had no runners in the last 14 days — the going flag is UNKNOWN and there is zero form to analyse, making this an entirely speculative runner whose impact depends wholly on raw ability revealed on debut.

runners_data.name: Harana
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partners D K Weld's four-year-old who holds a 0W2P record from three runs including a second on soft going at 8f; racing prominently at OR 72, Weld's horses tend to arrive fit and this horse's style suits sitting close to Mano Chicago — the most naturally placed of any runner given the race's lone-leader shape.

races.paceDynamic: Mano Chicago is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Ben Coen can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m1½f trip on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe. Harana is the only other horse with any interest in racing prominently, and with Coen's mount likely to stride straight to the front uncontested, the pace will be measured rather than fierce — favouring a horse with tactical speed to track it rather than one coming from the clouds. The field is saturated with hold-up types: Believe Again, Coul Dreamer, Western Bandit, and Cuckaloo Hill are all true hold-up horses shuffled forward on the map because the rear is overcrowded, meaning several riders will be fighting for space at the back rather than finding a clean passage. This race shape — a lone leader setting a modest, uncontested gallop — strongly favours a prominent or close-tracking profile that can sit within two lengths of Mano Chicago, make the move at the turn, and quicken on ground that rewards a clean, economical run rather than a late, wide sweep.

scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Mano Chicago is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a measured pace that suits the front end.
scenarios.body: If Mano Chicago is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a measured pace that suits the front end.

watchPoints.text: Harana is the only horse with the profile and position to exploit Mano Chicago's controlled gallop directly — Chris Hayes is likely to slot in second and the Weld yard's fitness record makes this the most dangerous rival to the pace-setter.

The hold-up group — Believe Again, Western Bandit, Coul Dreamer, and Cuckaloo Hill — will all converge at the rear at the start; watch for crowding and interference in the early stages as these horses compete for the same space.

Mano Chicago wears a hood and is stepping up markedly in trip from its 10f base to 1m1½f; if the hood fails to settle the horse and it runs too freely in front, the steady gallop assumption collapses and the race shape changes entirely.

Drowsy Maggie is a complete unknown on debut for a yard with no recent runners — Nathan Crosse could be sitting on anything, and punters should monitor market moves in the minutes before post time for any stable confidence signals.

Take Me's tongue-tie and unknown-style flag combined with Colin Keane's booking for Noel Meade suggests connections believe the horse has untapped ability — watch where Keane positions the horse in the first two furlongs as a guide to its likely running style.

races.name: Michael Joyce Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Daler
runners_data.note: Front-runner for G M Lyons with Colin Keane booked — a strong retrieval pairing — racing over a trip 3f longer than recent starts but the soft-ground win in last run fits today's conditions; the STYLE_FIT flag is a quirk of the map rather than a concern here as he is the natural leader.

runners_data.name: Grey Leader
runners_data.note: 58-day absence is a significant flag for this Nicola Burns (5lb claim) ride; has a genuine hold-up style and one career win on good ground, though sim-going stats (10/15) are encouraging — needs things to fall right from the rear on a track that rarely suits pure closers.

runners_data.name: Mocking
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners a horse whose 1/10f/SOF win is the standout relevant form reference — genuine hold-up horse for J P Murtagh who has been firing (4/22 in 14 days); 50-day break is worth monitoring but Murtagh runners return fit and the trip is ideal.

runners_data.name: Dark Summit
runners_data.note: Consistent fader in finishes and zero wins or places on good or better going in recent history — the ⚠ fade flag is well-earned and nothing in this profile suggests a reversal; Seamie Heffernan's presence adds class but the material is limited.

runners_data.name: Dark Viper
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides a prominent-style horse whose best recent run was a win on heavy and an OR-competitive effort on soft; 18-day turnaround, tongue-tie in place, and the style fits this race shape well — the most credible challenger to Daler in the early stages.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners a mare with a sharp turn of form — 1st and 4th in last two — and a genuine hold-up pedigree; she is a true closer redistributed into midfield because of traffic at the rear, so her natural position is further back than shown and she will need the pace to be honest to deliver late.

runners_data.name: Justenzia
runners_data.note: Denis Gerard Hogan's second string, having run just 11 days ago; a prominent rider in Chris Hayes, but the horse's recent form (0-0) and a distance record showing better over longer trips (13f, 12f) make this a query at 1m1½f.

runners_data.name: Merlin The Wizard
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride on a horse who won over 12f last time — that form is at a longer trip, and his true hold-up style means he is working against the grain of this race shape; the redistribution into midfield on the map reflects the crowded rear, not his preference.

runners_data.name: Storm Averted
runners_data.note: 244 days off the track is a serious concern — the last run was August — and while there is a tongue-tie for conditions specialist Maurice Ahern, the lengthy absence combined with a hold-up style that has been pushed up the map makes this a speculative proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Flying Fortress
runners_data.note: Jack Kearney (3lb claim) on a Gavin Cromwell prominent type with a win two runs back over 8f on heavy; the step up in trip to 1m1½f is new territory and the tongue-tie is fitted again, but the style fits the expected race shape and the yard is in a productive spell (4/42 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Lough Leane
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good last time for Maurice Ahern — the same yard as Storm Averted — but the natural hold-up style places Lough Leane among those displaced from the rear of the field; STYLE_FIT discount applies, and the 18-day return interval keeps the horse fresh if not at peak.

races.paceDynamic: Daler is the one confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to push him hard for the lead, he should settle into a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Yielding ground over 1m1½f at Ballinrobe. Dark Viper and Flying Fortress are the most credible prominent challengers who will look to sit close to Daler's heels, meaning the early pace is unlikely to be truly searching — expect a steady-to-moderate tempo that compresses the field and makes it harder for true hold-up horses to generate meaningful momentum late. The going is consistently Good to Yielding across the card, which adds a small stamina premium without turning it into a true slog, favouring horses that can travel comfortably mid-to-prominently and produce a sustained finish rather than a sudden burst. This race shape firmly favours the prominent-to-midfield profile: a controlled pace from one leader, a bunched field through the middle stages, and a finish where those travelling sweetly just off the pace hold a decisive edge over genuine hold-up horses — several of whom (Marmeladova, Merlin The Wizard, Storm Averted, Lough Leane) are redistributed into midfield on the map because the field holds more natural hold-up types than can realistically get to the rear of the field in a race this size, with Daler and Dark Viper most certain to actually secure their forward positions.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Dark Viper (Shane Foley) or Flying Fortress (Jack Kearney) attempts to push past Daler in the early stages — any pressure on Daler's lead would transform the pace profile from controlled to searching and radically change the finish-shape.

Merlin The Wizard, Storm Averted and Lough Leane are all genuine hold-up horses forced further forward than they want to be — if they get stuck three-wide in midfield traffic through the middle stages, their finishing kick will be severely blunted.

Grey Leader returns after 58 days with no 14-day trainer form on record — monitor in the paddock and at the start for any signs of freshness or lack of peak fitness before committing to this runner in any scenario.

Storm Averted's 244-day layoff for Maurice Ahern is the longest absence in the field — watch how Nathan Crosse settles the horse in the early stages, as a fresh hold-up type may race too keenly and undermine its own late run.

The going is consistently Good to Yielding across all seven races on the card, suggesting the strip has not changed materially during the evening — but horses drawn wider at Ballinrobe can find themselves covering extra ground on a tight circuit, worth noting for those expected to race prominently from wide draws.

races.name: J.J. Burke Peugeot Handicap

runners_data.name: Sands Castle
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides, but this OR-60 filly has shown a pattern of fading in the closing stages across recent starts, posting zeros at her last two outings, and with no improvement in form over this distance on good-ish ground she looks vulnerable in a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Onyeisi
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes over for Karl Thornton and this colt has a solid recent run at 10f on good ground; the tongue tie is noted and his sim-going form (4/13 in similar conditions) suggests he handles the surface without excelling — a mid-division hold-up horse who will need a clear run late.

runners_data.name: Flagstone Lady
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a significant booking for M D O'Callaghan but this filly has only three runs to her name, all on faster ground, and the fade-in-finish flag is a real concern; with a crawl tempo likely she will need to produce a sharper finish than she has managed so far.

runners_data.name: A Pretty Penny
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan rides for Deborah Cody, and this filly's one win came over exactly this trip and surface type (1/10f/GOO), making her statistically the most relevant form-fit in the race; OR 54 and 134lbs is manageable and she holds the best sim-going profile of the leading contenders.

runners_data.name: Tavarua
runners_data.note: Tongue tie applied, ran badly at odds-on last time (9th, OR 53) and is genuinely a hold-up horse who will be racing out of her natural position if pushed forward in this field — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 is a real discount, and three runs without a placing on similar ground underline the concern.

runners_data.name: Brave Approach
runners_data.note: Jarlath Fahey's runner returns just 10 days after his last start, and while he managed a win on Standard ground (1/8f/STA), his turf form on soft and good is modest — a true hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield means he is unlikely to get an ideal run in a race with no pace.

runners_data.name: Rodeo Blues
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is a high-quality booking for Joseph O'Brien's yard, which posts a strong 14-day strike rate (9/63), but this colt has never won in five tries and his soft-ground form (6/9f/SOF being his best) gives him some going relevance; the fade flag and redistribution mean his natural game won't be easily expressed here.

runners_data.name: Connova
runners_data.note: Robbie Colgan picks up the ride for Sheila Lavery and the filly showed a flash of ability when fourth over 10f on Good earlier in the season; she is a genuine hold-up type shuffled forward on the map, and her best position in a slow-run race will be to travel comfortably in the pack and hope for a clear lane.

runners_data.name: Cause I Like You
runners_data.note: Tongue-and-trip headgear (tp), trained by Michael Mulvany who is 3/17 in 14 days suggesting a live yard; last six runs have produced a best of 4th and he stretches to 8f here from shorter trips — the longer distance may help, and a clean run from an open pace could suit him more than his current form implies.

runners_data.name: Perggosa
runners_data.note: Keith Henry Clarke's filly returns after 72 days off, the longest break in the field, which is a significant unknown; her three runs have all come on softer ground (SOF/STA) and she has not shown enough to suggest the layoff has been used to solve her problems — the fade flag and fitness query make her one to oppose.

runners_data.name: Canon Law
runners_data.note: Robyn Donaghue-Leahy claims 7lbs which brings the weight down meaningfully, but Canon Law has finished outside the frame in four of five starts with a solitary 5th as best; a genuine hold-up type now mapped to midfield, the apprentice claim may be the only real angle here.

runners_data.name: Sand Art
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes rides for Kevin Coleman (1/11 in 14 days) and this filly's form over 7f and shorter is unremarkable; she steps up slightly in trip here but the fade flag and a best recent finish of 7th suggest she lacks the finishing kick this sprint-finish scenario will demand.

runners_data.name: Wedding Year
runners_data.note: Tongue tie applied and Cillian Rowan claims 10lbs, which is a chunky allowance for Adrian McGuinness's runner; she placed third on Standard at 8f suggesting some ability, but her Good-ground form is poor (13th, 11th) and she is a true hold-up type asked to race out of role.

runners_data.name: Honey Dale
runners_data.note: Rory Mulligan claims 5lbs for Paul Mulligan in what is a small yard entry (0/2 in 14 days); the filly posted a fifth over 7f on Good and a fifth on Soft, showing minor ability, and her redistribution to midfield from a true hold-up role is unlikely to be damaging if she travels smoothly in the pack — she is the least exposed of the lower-rated fill.

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany's runner (yard 2/17 in 14 days) runs just four days after his last start, which is unusually quick and worth monitoring for freshness; his sim-going profile is intriguing (8 runs on soft, 4th being his best twice) and he handles this ground well — a hold-up type forced forward on the map who could prove dangerous if he drifts into a prominent berth naturally.

races.paceDynamic: This is an unusual race in that every single runner is catalogued as a hold-up type, meaning there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse expected to set a genuine early gallop. With 15 runners over 1m1½f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe and nobody willing to lead, the field is likely to dawdle in the early stages before bunching and erupting into a cavalry charge in the straight — a sprint finish from a slow crawl. That dynamic compresses the field, eliminates positional advantage almost entirely, and places a premium on horses who can quicken sharply off a slow pace from a handy position — those who can get to the front of the pack at the two-furlong pole without being trapped wide or pocketed will have a decisive edge. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can physically place at the rear — Tavarua, Nephin Mountain, Rodeo Blues, Brave Approach, Connova, Cause I Like You, Perggosa, Canon Law, Sand Art, Wedding Year and Honey Dale are all redistributed to midfield, but in a race with no true pace, the horses who drift forward voluntarily from that group and secure a prominent pitch at the business end will be best placed. In this shape, the profile that benefits most is a horse carrying a low weight with tactical versatility, good form at the distance and trip on give in the ground, who can travel handy and produce a decisive burst — the higher-rated hold-up types with proven form at this trip (A Pretty Penny, Onyeisi, Nephin Mountain) command closest attention.

watchPoints.text: With no confirmed pace-setter in a 15-runner field, watch for Nephin Mountain and Cause I Like You drifting forward from the redistributed midfield group to accidentally secure a prominent position — if either finds themselves on the lead after two furlongs without exerting any energy, they become instantly dangerous.

A Pretty Penny's proven form at exactly this trip and going profile makes her the standout shape-fit, but Seamie Heffernan will need to navigate a congested early crawl without getting pocketed — a wide draw or clean passage is essential; watch her position at the two-furlong pole.

The Going Report consistently describes this course as Good to Yielding (not the Good to Soft listed in the race header) — if the ground is softer than anticipated, horses with the fade-in-finish flag (Sands Castle, Flagstone Lady, Tavarua, Brave Approach, Rodeo Blues) are at heightened risk of emptying dramatically in the final furlong.

Perggosa returns after a 72-day absence — longer than any other runner — and her fitness level relative to horses who are race-fit off recent starts is a genuine unknown; watch her market move in the final hour as a guide to stable confidence.

Dylan Browne McMonagle on Rodeo Blues for the Joseph O'Brien yard (9/63 in 14 days) is the most significant trainer-jockey combination in terms of recent strike rate — even if the horse is a pace-map mismatch, this pairing routinely finds winners and deserves monitoring if the race develops chaotically.

races.name: GAIN The Advantage Series Handicap

runners_data.name: Dutch Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Noel Meade who has finished ninth on his last two starts; suited by this going but the ⚠ fade-in-finish flag and recent poor form make him hard to recommend despite being on a manageable mark of OR 69.

runners_data.name: Daboya

races.paceDynamic: Daboya is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 17-horse field over 1m5f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe, and with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, Sam Coen's mount should control proceedings at a sustainable, tempo-regulated gallop throughout. The prominent types — Barrogstown Girl, Coulstys Way, Lagoon Nebula, Eternal Echo, Miss Gitana, and Makaiah — will fill the positions just off Daboya, creating an organised, strung-out pack rather than a contested early pace. Several horses labelled hold-up types (Sonic Invader, Bruant, Miss Crinshawn, Miss Australie, Covert Legend) have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field's genuine hold-up contingent is deeper than the pace shape can accommodate at the rear; of those, Sonic Invader (Colin Keane) and Miss Crinshawn (Ben Coen) have the jockey firepower most likely to secure a better-than-natural berth. With one uncontested pace-setter on testing ground over a truly stamina-demanding trip, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Daboya's manageable fractions and quicken from a handy position in the straight, rather than closers who will face a wall of traffic after being shuffled back.

watchPoints.text: Barrogstown Girl's long absence (244 days) is offset by a perfect course-and-distance profile — watch the market closely; if she opens short she is a serious threat to everything prominent in this shape.

Colin Keane on Sonic Invader is the single biggest jockey upgrade in the race; despite being a redistributed hold-up type, Keane can manufacture a handy position and the horse's consistent 3rd-3rd at 14-16f on good ground makes this a live threat across scenarios.

Daboya controls the pace and any sign of him being pressed or overhauling rivals before the straight would dramatically change the shape — watch the early stalls and first furlong closely to see if any prominent types force a faster gallop.

Wolf Prince is aged 10 but both course wins at 16f on soft ground are directly relevant to tonight's conditions; if the ground softens further through the card he becomes markedly more dangerous for the staying scenarios.

Miss Gitana carries the Dylan Browne McMonagle booking at a low OR, but the ⚠ fade flag and 0W from 15 runs at sim-going suggest any market move should be treated with caution rather than followed blindly.

runners_data.name: Royal Hollow
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old trained and ridden by Andrew Slattery returning from a 284-day absence (23 runs on that layoff marker); her historical record of 3 wins and 9 places from 15 sim-going runs over 16-17f is the most compelling stamina and ground profile in the field, and she ran 2nd last time on Good over 17f.

runners_data.name: Denim And Diamonds
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the mount for Joseph Patrick O'Brien on this hold-up filly who has finished 7th, 8th or 10th in each of her last four starts; the tongue tie is noted and while sim-going figures show 1 win from 10, she needs something dramatic to change on current form.

runners_data.name: Switch From Diesel

runners_data.name: Thatwilldoso

runners_data.name: Earthsong
runners_data.note: McDonogh partners this McCreery four-year-old who carries the lightest weight and arrives on a career-best last-time-out win over 14f on Good — the genuine hold-up horse in this field and racing entirely in role; sim-going figures of 1 win and 2 places from 8 runs, last run 33 days ago, all point to a horse in form.

runners_data.name: La Dame Blanche
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by style but remapped to midfield given the rear of the field is also crowded with type; Joyce takes the 3lb claim for Kilmartin whose T14 record is 0/1 — a seven-year-old whose sim-going form reads 1 win and 3 places from 15 runs, though recent figures of 4-7-9 at shorter trips are modest.

races.paceDynamic: Deressa is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of eight over 1m5f on Good To Yielding ground at Ballinrobe, and with no genuine rival likely to contest the early lead, she can dictate a measured, controlled tempo entirely on her own terms. Royal Hollow and Stellar Quality are the most natural prominent horses and will look to sit close to Deressa without forcing the pace, meaning the early gallop is unlikely to be pressured. Switch From Diesel, Thatwilldoso, and La Dame Blanche are all genuine prominent or hold-up types who cannot all occupy their preferred positions — Switch From Diesel and Thatwilldoso are most likely to secure closer berths given their recent form and ratings, while La Dame Blanche may be forced to settle deeper than ideal. With a single uncontested pace-setter and a sustainable tempo over this stamina trip on testing ground, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace and quicken at a measured tempo — horses with confirmed stamina and clean prominent/hold-up profiles racing in role.

watchPoints.text: Royal Hollow returns from 284 days off but boasts the deepest stamina and going profile in the race — watch whether Slattery has her ready to run a big first-day-back over her optimum trip.

Earthsong is the one horse racing in role as a hold-up type on a career-best mark and with a recent win over 14f on Good — watch her position at halfway; if she is tracking within five lengths of the lead she is a serious late threat.

Switch From Diesel is back from 232 days absent and is a natural front-runner who cannot get that position today — watch whether Keane elects to push her up early regardless, which would fundamentally alter the pace shape if she challenges Deressa.

The pace is entirely in Deressa's hands; if she is allowed to coast through the first mile at a crawl, the race becomes a sprint home and her rivals' measured positioning counts for nothing — watch the early fractions carefully.

La Dame Blanche's jockey Wesley Joyce claims 3lbs but the trainer Kilmartin has only one runner in the T14 window — a low-key booking on a horse remapped from her natural position, worth monitoring only if the pace collapses and she gets a soft lead into a staying finish.
